purpose: This shows a function as a machine: one input goes in and exactly one output comes out. You can see it as a rule, a table and a graph at once, and use the vertical line test to tell a function from a rule that is not one.

stops.title: Machine and graph
stops.text: At the top is the function machine: input (green), rule, output (red). Below is the graph. Drag in the graph, or tap a table row, to pick an input. The green dashed line marks the input, the red one the output.
stops.try: Drag across the graph and watch the machine show a new input and output.

stops.title: Choose a rule
stops.text: Four rules are functions: three straight lines and x squared. The fifth is a circle, which is not a function. For the circle, one input gives two outputs and the machine shows both.
stops.try: Pick the circle, then pick x squared. How do the outputs differ?

stops.title: Choose an input
stops.text: This slider picks the input x, from a few set values. It does the same as dragging on the graph or tapping a table row. The readout names the output, or both outputs for the circle.
stops.try: Set x to 0 and then to 3 for the circle and compare the outputs.

stops.title: Table and points
stops.text: Shows a table of inputs and outputs, and plots each row as a point on the graph. The highlighted row is your current input. Tap a row to select it. The graph is all these points joined up.
stops.try: Turn it on, tap a row, and find the matching point.

stops.title: Vertical line test
stops.text: Draws a violet vertical line at your input and counts how many times it crosses the graph. A function crosses once at every input. The circle crosses twice, so it fails the test.
stops.try: Turn it on with the circle and drag across. Where does it cross once?

stops.title: Equal steps
stops.text: Marks steps of the same size along the input (green) and shows how the output changes each time (red). For a straight line the output steps are always the same. For x squared they are not.
stops.try: Turn it on for 2x - 1, then pick x squared and compare the steps.

stops.title: Step size
stops.text: Changes how far apart the inputs are, from 1 to 3. For a line, a bigger input step gives a proportionally bigger output step. Moving it turns on Equal steps for you.
stops.try: Set the step to 2 on the line 2x - 1. How big is the output step now?

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Two questions at the end. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project step 2 and ask: how many outputs does x = 3 have, and what does the violet line tell us? Students often think any graph is a function, or that a function must be a straight line, so also show x squared. Step 4 sets up slope as a constant change.
